newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/mark up, dlr/yen steady after Rubin as US ends. [CORRECTED 01:40 GMT 11/4]
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark up, dlr/yen steady after Rubin as US ends. [CORRECTED 01:40 GMT 11/4]

text.p: Dollar/mark ended higher while dollar/yen was unchanged though still shaky after Japan's Finance Ministry and Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said they were concerned about its recent strength.

Worries about central bank dollar sales weighed on the dollar again in New York, particularly in the wake of Rubin's Televised remarks on CNBC where for the first time he said the United States shared Japan's concern about the weak yen.

"They (Japan) are concerned ... about combatting excessive weakness with intervention and one can infer that he (Rubin) also shares their whole concern about the situation," said David Gilmore, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.
The dollar closed unchanged from its open at 125.70/80 yen but rose to 1.7195/05 marks, from 1.7150/60.
However, Rubin stressed that the United States' had not abandoned its policy of advocating a strong dollar, which initially gave the dollar a brief lift.
"Our policy is absolutely unchanged," Rubin said in answer to a question about possible market confusion on U.S. policy.

In Tokyo, the dollar rallied to 127.16 yen (corrects from 127.10 yen), its highest level since August 1992, before Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka was quoted as saying that recent yen moves were obviously excessive, which the market took as a warning that Japan would try to curb the dollar's rise.
Dollar/mark failed to hold above 1.72 after remarks by German finance officials lifted it from the 1.7121 low hit after dollar/yen dragged it off a retest of 1.7270.
"It's basically just following dollar/yen down," said Kisoo Park, a senior foreign exchange dealer at Bank of Boston.
Juergen Stark, the German State Secretary to the Finance Ministry said a dollar exchange rate over 1.72 marks was part of a normal correction.
Meanwhile, Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said recent dollar moves were not sensational, given the relative strength of the U.S. economy compared to Germany's.
In other trade, the dollar was at 1.4690/00 Swiss francs compared to 1.4692/02. It rose to Canadian $1.3943/48 from C$1.3905/10.
The pound rose to $1.6225/35 from $1.6205/15 and the Australian dollar rose to $0.7855/60 from $0.7803/08.
